name: _syscall
description: The _syscall macros generate wrapper functions to invoke system calls directly without library support. They are used by specifying the return type, name, and arguments of the desired system call. This feature is obsolete and has been removed from modern Linux headers.

parameters.name: X
parameters.description: Number of arguments for the system call (0-6)

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The return type of the system call

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the system call

parameters.name: type1
parameters.description: The type of the first argument

parameters.name: arg1
parameters.description: The name of the first argument

parameters.name: type2
parameters.description: The type of the second argument (if applicable)

parameters.name: arg2
parameters.description: The name of the second argument (if applicable)

return_value.success: Returns the result of the system call if nonnegative
return_value.failure: Returns -1 and sets errno to the absolute value of the negative result

bugs: The _syscall macros do not produce a prototype, which may cause issues for C++ users, and argument types must be passed by value or pointer. They are obsolete and removed from modern headers.
